newsitem.title: UK: Shorts of Belfast to create 1,000 new jobs.
newsitem.headline: Shorts of Belfast to create 1,000 new jobs.

text.p: Belfast planemaker Short Rovers Plc said on Wednesday it will create 1,000 jobs over five years from work on two new aircraft programmes for the Bombardier Inc aerospace group.

Shorts, which is part of the group, said it expects to employ 750 workers on design and component manufacture for the newly-launched 70-seat Canadair regional jet series 700 and 250 workers on a major work package for the new 70-seat de Havilland Dash 8-400 turbo prop regional airliner.
The Canadair jet contract was announced last month but Shorts said on Wednesday that the original employment target of 600 had now been increased by 150.

Roy McNulty, chairman of Shorts, said the jobs boost would create more than the employment losses suffered by Shorts after the collapse of a contract with Dutch plane maker Fokker which went bankrupt last year.

Short Brothers, which is part of Montreal-based Bombardier Inc., would break new ground in the regional aircraft market in terms of aircraft performance and operating costs, McNulty said in a statement.

"Our extensive involvement on the programmes is excellent news for the company and for Northern Ireland and marks the continued growth of our Bombardier aircraft business which, since privatisation, has grown from nothing in 1989 to 150 million sterling a year now," McNulty said.

"Provided programme rates across the rest of our business remain constant, we expect that these two aircraft programmes could create 1,000 new jobs in Belfast over the next five years. We would in effect be creating more jobs than we lost last year following the collapse of Fokker."
Bombardier acquired Shorts in a privatisation deal in 1989. Short Brothers has 9,000 employees world wide in aero structures, aviation support services and close air defence systems.
Shorts said that it would undertake design and manufacturing work on the forward and central fuselage and the engine nacelle system in the Canadair regional jet series 700 airliner.
It had also been selected to design engine nacelles, wing-mounted flight control surfaces and main landing gear fairings for the de Havilland Dash 8-400 airliner.
Bombardier aerospace group is the world's fourth largest civil aircraft manufacturer.
Bombardier's revenues for its last financial year ended January 31, 1996 totalled 7.1 billion Canadian dollars and more than 85 percent of those revenues were generated in markets outside Canada.
